Also asserted inside the generator (§B L6 SD-S4 solves the contact-effect θ to land in this band). Asserting it here as well means a generator change that drifts the baseline cannot pass silently.

That is a ceiling on this criterion, not a prediction of it: the model reads those latents only through noisy observables and will land below it.

criteria.rationale: The shape of the precision curve either side of the operating budget, with CIs. A curve that is flat between 5% and 20% would mean the ranking is not doing much, whatever the single headline number says.
criteria.note: REPORTED, NO TARGET — the plan pre-registers a band at 10% only.

result.detail: side budgets either side of the 10% operating point; the interval on each cell is the 5-seed spread where one exists, not a confidence interval

criteria.rationale: Per-product windows are a mentor mandate: a gold-loan lead is worthless on day three, a home-loan lead is alive for a fortnight. If the model pitches a one-day product to people who take a fortnight to close, the window it prints beside the lead does not describe the product it is selling.
criteria.note:
WHAT THIS MEASURES: conversion timing among converters. Of the held-out customers inside the contact budget who do disburse, the share whose disbursement falls within the pre-registered window of the product the model offered them (see label_definition.conversion_windows_days). A conversion that lands outside the offered product's window counts against this criterion even though it is a real disbursement.
WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is NOT contact-SLA compliance. It does not measure whether a relationship manager made contact before the lead's contact_by expired, and it never should be quoted as if it did. Nothing in this pipeline observes an RM dialling — there are no contact timestamps in the delivered pack — so contact-SLA compliance is unmeasured. The earlier phrasing ("the RM queue's SLA") was wrong and is retired.
INTERPRETATION: the plan introduces "window respect" without defining it; the definition above is this pack's registration of it. The threshold is unchanged from pre-registration.

result.detail: SK-04 measures CONVERSION TIMING AMONG CONVERTERS — of the selected rows that disbursed, the share that disbursed inside the offered product's window. It is NOT contact-SLA compliance. Interval is the 5-SEED SPREAD (2.5-97.5 percentile across the registered seeds, criteria.yaml confidence.cross_seed) — training-seed variability, NOT a confidence interval around the packed seed; 5-seed mean 0.8813; the packed seed's own value (0.9009) lies outside this spread, which is expected of a 5-point percentile interval and is not a defect | packed seed (0.9009) passes this band; the 5-seed mean (0.8813) fails it — reported, not hidden. CONTACT-SLA COMPLIANCE (reported, never graded; `data/experiments/event_triggered.json`). SK-04 does not measure this and must not be quoted as if it did. Simulated dialling over the delivered queue on one shared calendar, weekends excluded, capacity sized to clear the busiest month. For NEWLY ABANDONED ONE-DAY products (personal, gold): today's monthly batch reaches 0.0067 of them in time at same-day ingestion and 0.0 with an overnight lag, because 0.9866 of those leads have a window that shut before the batch produced them (median 27.0 days from abandonment to call). Scoring on the abandonment EVENT instead takes that to 0.6303 at same-day ingestion and 0.4622 with an overnight lag; a three-day lag returns it to 0.0 because three days is longer than a one-day window. Under a halved calling capacity the event regime falls to 0.014 with a p90 of 232.0 days, so capacity dominates the trigger once the queue is overloaded. POST-CONTACT DISBURSEMENT is reported separately at 0.3445 and is deliberately NOT derived from the SLA: the generator's label has no decay after contact_by, so this simulation cannot price what late contact costs in conversions. Only a pilot with real contact-time-to-outcome data can.

criteria.rationale: Window-shopper detection is the feature that keeps RM time away from tyre-kickers. Deliberately a modest floor: the generator makes the signal informative but NOT deterministic (§B L6 SD-S3 — some genuine buyers balk at the fee once), so a high AUC here would mean the synthetic data had made the problem too easy.
criteria.note: AUC against the generator's latent window_shopper flag on the held-out book.

result.detail: Interval is the packed seed's own 95% hanley-mcneil confidence interval (row-level; no cross-seed spread for this metric)

criteria.rationale: A prospecting model is retrained on a cadence but used continuously. Losing more than 5 percentage points of precision on later months means the queue goes stale faster than the bank can refresh it.
criteria.note: Measured in PERCENTAGE POINTS (holdout precision@10% minus out-of-time precision@10%), not as a ratio. Improvement is reported as a negative degradation and passes.

criteria.rationale: Retrain the full pipeline on randomly permuted labels. Anything outside chance means the evaluation harness itself leaks — the strongest single check that the reported precision is real.
criteria.note: INTERPRETATION: the permutation is of the LABEL, with split, features and hyper-parameters untouched. Averaged over the registered seeds.

criteria.rationale: Which families actually carry the model — cross-bank transactions from API 595/739, salary-credit behaviour, dwell signals, journey friction, shopper signals. Reported so the "what would we lose without this API" question has an evidenced answer.

Baseline (all 69 features): precision@10%=0.2107 [0.1733, 0.2536], AUC=0.6522. delta_pp = baseline - ablated, in percentage points of precision@10% (positive = the family helps; negative = dropping it improved precision on this refit). 'product' drops the categorical that differentiates the six candidate rows per customer-month by construction, so its ablation is expected to collapse ranking rather than reveal a bug. Families whose ablated AUC rose ABOVE the baseline's own 95% Hanley-McNeil interval [0.6196, 0.6847] (i.e. dropping them helped beyond noise, which the L9 brief flags as worth a second look): ['product'].

criteria.rationale: Behaviour when the book shifts: consent withdrawal at scale, a suppression-rule sweep (§B L6 SD-S6), cross-bank transaction data (595/739) unavailable, and a doubled window-shopper share.

result.detail: small-book refit (n=1,778 customers, single seed 7 — see validation/runners/_refit.py). Baseline: precision@10%=0.2107 [0.1733, 0.2536], AUC=0.6522. delta_pp = scenario - baseline (positive = the scenario IMPROVED precision, negative = it degraded). 2x base rate: 681 duplicate positive training rows added to the fit split only, scored against the unduplicated held population — precision@10%=0.2259. channel-missing (contact): ['contacts_30d', 'contacts_90d', 'campaign_contacts_6m', 'last_contact_days', 'last_campaign_matches_product'] blanked to NaN in a copy of the SAME fitted baseline ranker's scoring frame (no retrain) — precision@10%=0.2107. Registered scenarios NOT computed this pass (reason: each needs a second generator run under altered parameters, which the refit budget does not cover twice over — not approximated, not silently dropped): ['consent withdrawal at scale', 'suppression-rule sweep (plan §B L6 SD-S6)']. FULL-SIZE CHALLENGE REGIMES (reported, no band; `data/experiments/challenge_regimes.json`). The development generator config is frozen to `data/experiments/frozen_generator.json` BEFORE any regime runs, one model is fitted on the development world at model seed 7 and NEVER refitted, and every challenge world uses generator seed 20270131, which the development world never used — so a degradation cannot be a training-split accident. Development world precision@10% = 0.2906. Regimes: source_latency 0.2693 (lift 2.84, +2.13 pp vs development); extra_missingness 0.2683 (lift 2.83, +2.23 pp vs development); macro_shock 0.2926 (lift 3.09, -0.20 pp vs development); customer_turnover 0.2649 (lift 2.84, +2.57 pp vs development); fresh_world 0.2751 (lift 3.0, +0.00 pp vs fresh_world); base_rate_half 0.2387 (lift 2.74, +3.64 pp vs fresh_world); base_rate_double 0.2689 (lift 3.01, +0.62 pp vs fresh_world); signal_correlation 0.2938 (lift 3.36, -1.87 pp vs fresh_world). Read each against its own control: a regenerated world is compared with `fresh_world` (same frozen config, new seed) because it has already paid the cost of being a new world. LIFT STABILITY: precision/baseline stays in [2.74, 3.36] across every regime — absolute precision tracks whatever base rate a world has, and the ratio is the part that belongs to the model. Any rupee figure derived from these numbers is a SIMULATION RESULT and the JSON carries an assumption range rather than a point.

criteria.rationale: Four-fifths rule on the contact rate: least-contacted group ÷ most-contacted group within each protected-proxy attribute, at the live contact budget.
criteria.source: plan §B L9 bands ("fairness incl. the documented gig failure")
criteria.note: REPORTED, NOT GATED. SANKET excludes gender, religion, caste, marital status and pin-code outright by policy (src/score_and_pack.py EXCLUDED_FEATURES), so the protected-proxy attributes evaluated are occupation_segment, income_band, city_tier and age band. The 0.80 reference line is the conventional four-fifths threshold, recorded so the report can say how far each attribute sits from it.

result.detail: four-fifths ratio = group selection rate / best group's selection rate in the same dim, at the live 10% contact budget, over the eligible snapshot population (`model.metrics.fairness_table`). Protected proxies evaluated: Segment (occupation), City tier, Age band, Income band — gender/religion/caste/marital status/pin-code are excluded outright by policy and are not in the data at all (`model.copy.EXCLUDED_FEATURES`). BELOW the 0.80 four-fifths line (reported, not softened): [('Segment', 'gig', 0.69), ('Income band', 'Q1 lowest', 0.79)]. Occupation segment 'gig': selection rate 7.61% vs the best group's rate, ratio 0.69 (n=815) — FAILS the 0.80 line. This is `criteria.yaml` SK-23's documented gig failure; severity is `report` in criteria.yaml (never gates the run), and the ratio is carried through here exactly as measured, never rounded up or excluded. Supplementary, non-gated equal-opportunity (TPR = contact rate among true potential-disbursers) exhibit on the SMALL book's own snapshot month (n_positives=84, single seed 7 — too few positives per cell for a production-grade read, hence not registered or gated): max-min TPR gap by dim = {'Segment': 0.022, 'City tier': 0.2, 'Age band': 0.194, 'Income band': 0.214}. criteria.yaml SK-23 registers only adverse_impact_ratio, not a TPR-gap band; this is reported for a human, not graded. DIAGNOSIS (`data/experiments/fairness_probe.json`, held-out split, not the snapshot, so the ratios differ from the graded value above): gig contact ratio 0.5681 against an OUTCOME ratio of 0.8992 — the queue amplifies that gap by 1.583x. The gig workers it does select convert 4.77 pp better than the salaried ones it selects, which is a stricter effective threshold, not a weaker population. Mean SHAP most against gig at the contact boundary: is_dropoff_product (-0.104), journey_stated_income_ratio (-0.096), journey_last_product_matches (-0.042), journey_fee_balk (-0.037). The retired 0.65/0.35 capacity blend, which was the ranking the queue actually delivered until 2026-09-21, scored a gig ratio of 0.21 on this same split — far worse than the 0.5681 the probability ranking gives, and worse than SK-23 ever reported, because SK-23 has always been measured on the probability list. REMEDIES, PRICED: blend, capacity weight 0.15 -> precision 0.2779 (costs 1.27 pp), gig ratio 0.45; blend, capacity weight 0.35 -> precision 0.2192 (costs 7.14 pp), gig ratio 0.21; equal selection rate per segment (ratio 1.00 by construction) -> precision 0.2892 (costs 0.14 pp), gig ratio 1.0; minimum four-fifths ratio 0.80 -> precision 0.2902 (costs 0.04 pp), gig ratio 0.8. Nothing was tuned to 0.80; the exchange rate is published so the choice stays a policy decision.

criteria.rationale: A known, accepted failure mode: irregular gig-economy income reads as instability to a model trained mostly on salaried credits, so gig workers are under-contacted. It is disclosed rather than tuned away, because tuning it away on synthetic data would be pretending to have solved it.
criteria.source: plan §B L9 bands ("fairness incl. the documented gig failure")
criteria.note: INTERPRETATION: registered as an existence check — the fairness section of REPORT.md must contain a quantified statement of the gig-worker gap, and it must be carried into the README's "What we did not build, and why". Kept at severity `report` because the plan lists it among reported findings; it is nonetheless a G5 honesty-gate item.

result.detail: quantified gig-worker statement: behavioural income estimate within +-15% for 76.4% of gig workers (n=254) vs 95.2% overall (n=1694); median error 8.7% gig vs 2.5% overall. Mechanism: irregular gig income reads as instability to a model trained mostly on salaried credits, which depresses the behavioural income estimate, which depresses the safe-EMI capacity score, which depresses rank — the chain MODEL_CARD.md §8 and the README's 'What we did not build, and why' both carry. Disclosed rather than tuned away: tuning it out on synthetic data would be pretending to have solved it.

criteria.rationale: Contextualises the gain: random contact, then balance-ranked contact (what a branch does today), then a logistic scorecard, then the LightGBM model, each with CI. If balance-ranking is within noise of the model, that is the honest finding and the deck says so.
criteria.note: The plan specifies runner 12 but pre-registers no band for it, so no threshold was invented. The rungs ARE pre-registered here so the comparison set cannot be chosen after the fact.

result.detail: four rungs, same held-out book, same 10% budget: [('random contact', 0.0948), ('balance-ranked (what a branch does today)', 0.0995), ('logistic scorecard', 0.2583), ('SANKET (one LightGBM, six products)', 0.2906)]. Rung-to-rung gaps: balance-ranking over random: +0.47 pp; logistic over balance-ranking: +15.88 pp; SANKET over logistic: +3.22 pp. If a rung is within noise of the next, that is the honest finding (criteria.yaml SK-25 rationale: 'If balance-ranking is within noise of the model, that is the honest finding and the deck says so').

amendments.change: DESCRIPTION ONLY. SK-04's threshold (>= 0.90), op, severity, runner, metric key and scope are all unchanged. What changed is the wording: the rationale used to say the criterion existed so "the RM queue's SLA" would not be "fiction", which reads as a claim that SK-04 measures whether a relationship manager made contact before the lead expired. It does not. It measures conversion timing among converters — of the held-out rows inside the contact budget that disbursed, the share that disbursed inside the offered product's window. The note now states that explicitly, and states that contact-SLA compliance is measured nowhere in this pack.
amendments.rationale: A third-party review (2026-09-21, §5) found the 90.1% being described as an operational contact-SLA result in the README, the model card and the cockpit. No contact timestamp exists in this pipeline, so that reading is unsupported by anything in the repo. The band itself was never the problem and is deliberately left where it was registered; loosening or retitling a metric because its description was wrong would be the exact move pre-registration exists to prevent.

SCOPING, NOT THRESHOLDS. No band moves. SK-01 stays [0.08, 0.10], SK-02 stays [0.25, 0.35], SK-18 stays [0.48, 0.52], SK-17 stays 0 — all `fail`, all with their ceilings. What is amended is the SCORING POPULATION SK-01 and SK-02 are computed over, which was under-specified at registration because this file was written before the application-journey layer (plan §B L6 SD-S2) existed and so before there was a drop-off population to name. The same entry re-points runner 07 at the files that layer actually emitted; SK-17 and SK-18 are listed only because that runner answers them, and neither band changes.

ORIGINAL WORDING (registered 2026-09-16T10:47:14+05:30). `label_definition.observation_unit`: "One (cust_id, month) row of the liability book at a snapshot month m. The model scores a consented customer as at m using only information available at or before m." `label_definition.primary.description`: "CONVERSION MEANS DISBURSEMENT, not lead creation and not application start (mentor mandate). 1 if, after being contacted at month m, the customer's application for the offered product reaches the Disburse stage within that product's pre-registered window; 0 otherwise, including applications that start and then abandon." `splits.holdout.scoring_population`: "Held-out, consented customers at the snapshot month. Precision-at-budget is computed on this population; the cockpit queue is built over the whole book but is never a measurement surface." `validation/runners/07_leakage.py` INPUTS: "data/application_journeys.csv  (PLANNED — plan §B L6 SD-S2)".

NEW WORDING. The scoring unit is a (customer, month) row for customers in the DROP-OFF POPULATION — consented, contactable customers with at least one abandoned application attempt in the trailing 12 months and no disbursement in flight — and the label is disbursement of any product within that product's decision window after an RM contact (windows in days: personal 1, gold 1, auto 3, education 7, home 14, lap 14 — unchanged, and unchanged from `conversion_windows_days` above). `random_contact_disbursement_rate` (SK-01) is the disbursement rate among a uniformly random 10% contact sample of that population. `precision_at_10pct_budget` (SK-02) is the same population, model-ranked at the same 10% contact budget. Runner 07's data path becomes `data/journeys.csv` + `data/journey_events.csv` (the alias columns SD-S2 emitted for the pre-registered spelling — cust_id, stage_reached, start_ts, abandon_ts, disburse_ts, blank_ratio, income_refused, revisit_count — stay); only the path and the column mapping change, not the leakage logic.
amendments.rationale: The mentors defined conversion as disbursement and said in terms that "the population that matters is the drop-offs". The RM-call baseline of 8-10% is a statement about CALLED PROSPECTS, not about every consented customer-month: on the whole book that rate is ~0.1% at a snapshot month (1.35% even at the three-month horizon the old pipeline measured), which would force the contact effect theta to a value no bank reviewer would accept in order to reach 8%. The business action being priced is an RM working a lead list, not ringing 60,000 savings customers, so the denominator has to be the lead list. Recorded as an amendment rather than applied as a reinterpretation because the population is part of what a pre-registered metric means, and changing it quietly — even without touching a threshold — is exactly the move pre-registration exists to prevent. Generator side: plan §B L6 SD-S4 solves theta against this population and asserts both bands in-script (`src/journeys/labels.py`, `check()`), across five seeds; `DATA_CARD.md` §12 documents the label, the two solved knobs and the known unrealisms that come with them.
